tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find).

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find).

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size stays on that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane) until you call this tool again with preset "desktop", so reset it once you are done testing. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent, 5 touch points, and mouse-to-touch translation (hover stops producing hover states). Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

=== build_release.bat ===
set WP=%CD%

set debug=OFF
set debuginfo=OFF
if "%1"=="debug" set debug=ON
if "%2"=="debug" set debug=ON
if "%1"=="debuginfo" set debuginfo=ON
if "%2"=="debuginfo" set debuginfo=ON
if "%debug%"=="ON" (
    set build_type=Debug
    set build_dir=build-dbg
) else (
    if "%debuginfo%"=="ON" (
        set build_type=RelWithDebInfo
        set build_dir=build-dbginfo
    ) else (
        set build_type=Release
        set build_dir=build
    )
)
echo build type set to %build_type%

cd deps
mkdir %build_dir%
cd %build_dir%
set DEPS=%CD%/OrcaSlicer_dep
set "SIG_FLAG="
if defined ORCA_UPDATER_SIG_KEY set "SIG_FLAG=-DORCA_UPDATER_SIG_KEY=%ORCA_UPDATER_SIG_KEY%"
if "%1"=="slicer" (
    GOTO :slicer
)
echo "building deps.."

echo cmake ../ -G "Visual Studio 16 2019" -A x64 -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=%build_type%
cmake ../ -G "Visual Studio 16 2019" -A x64 -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=%build_type%
cmake --build . --config %build_type% --target deps -- -m

if "%1"=="deps" exit /b 0

:slicer
echo "building Orca Slicer..."
cd %WP%
mkdir %build_dir%
cd %build_dir%

echo cmake .. -G "Visual Studio 16 2019" -A x64 -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=%build_type%
cmake .. -G "Visual Studio 16 2019" -A x64 -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=%build_type% %SIG_FLAG%
cmake --build . --config %build_type% --target ALL_BUILD -- -m
cd ..
call scripts/run_gettext.bat
cd %build_dir%
cmake --build . --target install --config %build_type%

=== build_release_vs.bat ===
@REM OrcaSlicer build script for Windows with VS auto-detect
@echo off
set WP=%CD%
set _START_TIME=%TIME%

@REM Default target architecture to the host CPU arch; override by passing
@REM "x64" or "arm64" as an argument. PROCESSOR_ARCHITEW6432 covers a 32-bit
@REM shell running on a 64-bit OS, where PROCESSOR_ARCHITECTURE reads "x86".
set arch=x64
if /I "%PROCESSOR_ARCHITECTURE%"=="ARM64" set arch=ARM64
if /I "%PROCESSOR_ARCHITEW6432%"=="ARM64" set arch=ARM64
if /I "%1"=="arm64" set arch=ARM64
if /I "%2"=="arm64" set arch=ARM64
if /I "%1"=="x64" set arch=x64
if /I "%2"=="x64" set arch=x64

@REM Check for Ninja Multi-Config option (-x)
set USE_NINJA=0
for %%a in (%*) do (
    if "%%a"=="-x" set USE_NINJA=1
)

if "%USE_NINJA%"=="1" (
    echo Using Ninja Multi-Config generator
    set CMAKE_GENERATOR="Ninja Multi-Config"
    set VS_VERSION=Ninja
    goto :generator_ready
)

@REM Detect Visual Studio version using msbuild
echo Detecting Visual Studio version using msbuild...

@REM Try to get MSBuild version - the output format varies by VS version
set VS_MAJOR=
for /f "tokens=*" %%i in ('msbuild -version 2^>^&1 ^| findstr /r "^[0-9][0-9]*\.[0-9][0-9]*\.[0-9][0-9]*"') do (
    for /f "tokens=1 delims=." %%a in ("%%i") do set VS_MAJOR=%%a
    set MSBUILD_OUTPUT=%%i
    goto :version_found
)

@REM Alternative method for newer MSBuild versions
if "%VS_MAJOR%"=="" (
    for /f "tokens=*" %%i in ('msbuild -version 2^>^&1 ^| findstr /r "[0-9][0-9]*\.[0-9][0-9]*\.[0-9][0-9]*"') do (
        for /f "tokens=1 delims=." %%a in ("%%i") do set VS_MAJOR=%%a
        set MSBUILD_OUTPUT=%%i
        goto :version_found
    )
)

:version_found
echo MSBuild version detected: %MSBUILD_OUTPUT%
echo Major version: %VS_MAJOR%

if "%VS_MAJOR%"=="" (
    echo Error: Could not determine Visual Studio version from msbuild
    echo Please ensure Visual Studio and MSBuild are properly installed
    exit /b 1
)

if "%VS_MAJOR%"=="16" (
    set VS_VERSION=2019
    set CMAKE_GENERATOR="Visual Studio 16 2019"
) else if "%VS_MAJOR%"=="17" (
    set VS_VERSION=2022
    set CMAKE_GENERATOR="Visual Studio 17 2022"
) else if "%VS_MAJOR%"=="18" (
    set VS_VERSION=2026
    set CMAKE_GENERATOR="Visual Studio 18 2026"
) else (
    echo Error: Unsupported Visual Studio version: %VS_MAJOR%
    echo Supported versions: VS2019 (16.x^), VS2022 (17.x^), VS2026 (18.x^)
    exit /b 1
)

echo Detected Visual Studio %VS_VERSION% (version %VS_MAJOR%)
echo Using CMake generator: %CMAKE_GENERATOR%

:generator_ready

@REM Pack deps
if "%1"=="pack" (
    setlocal ENABLEDELAYEDEXPANSION
    cd %WP%/deps/build
    if "%arch%"=="ARM64" cd %WP%/deps/build-arm64
    for /f "tokens=2-4 delims=/ " %%a in ('date /t') do set build_date=%%c%%b%%a
    echo packing deps: OrcaSlicer_dep_win-!arch!_!build_date!_vs!VS_VERSION!.zip

    %WP%/tools/7z.exe a OrcaSlicer_dep_win-!arch!_!build_date!_vs!VS_VERSION!.zip OrcaSlicer_dep
    if errorlevel 1 goto :failed
    goto :done
)

set debug=OFF
set debuginfo=OFF
if "%1"=="debug" set debug=ON
if "%2"=="debug" set debug=ON
if "%1"=="debuginfo" set debuginfo=ON
if "%2"=="debuginfo" set debuginfo=ON
if "%debug%"=="ON" (
    set build_type=Debug
    set build_dir=build-dbg
) else (
    if "%debuginfo%"=="ON" (
        set build_type=RelWithDebInfo
        set build_dir=build-dbginfo
    ) else (
        set build_type=Release
        set build_dir=build
    )
)
if "%arch%"=="ARM64" set build_dir=%build_dir%-arm64
echo build type set to %build_type%, arch=%arch%

setlocal DISABLEDELAYEDEXPANSION
cd deps
mkdir %build_dir%
cd %build_dir%
set "SIG_FLAG="
if defined ORCA_UPDATER_SIG_KEY set "SIG_FLAG=-DORCA_UPDATER_SIG_KEY=%ORCA_UPDATER_SIG_KEY%"

if "%1"=="slicer" (
    GOTO :slicer
)
echo "building deps.."

echo on
REM Set minimum CMake policy to avoid <3.5 errors
set CMAKE_POLICY_VERSION_MINIMUM=3.5
if "%USE_NINJA%"=="1" (
    cmake ../ -G %CMAKE_GENERATOR% -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=%build_type%
    if errorlevel 1 goto :failed
    cmake --build . --config %build_type% --target deps
    if errorlevel 1 goto :failed
) else (
    cmake ../ -G %CMAKE_GENERATOR% -A %arch% -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=%build_type%
    if errorlevel 1 goto :failed
    cmake --build . --config %build_type% --target deps -- -m
    if errorlevel 1 goto :failed
)
@echo off

if "%1"=="deps" goto :done

:slicer
echo "building Orca Slicer..."
cd %WP%
mkdir %build_dir%
cd %build_dir%

echo on
set CMAKE_POLICY_VERSION_MINIMUM=3.5
if "%USE_NINJA%"=="1" (
    cmake .. -G %CMAKE_GENERATOR% -DORCA_TOOLS=ON %SIG_FLAG% -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=%build_type%
    if errorlevel 1 goto :failed
    cmake --build . --config %build_type% --target ALL_BUILD
    if errorlevel 1 goto :failed
) else (
    cmake .. -G %CMAKE_GENERATOR% -A %arch% -DORCA_TOOLS=ON %SIG_FLAG% -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=%build_type%
    if errorlevel 1 goto :failed
    cmake --build . --config %build_type% --target ALL_BUILD -- -m
    if errorlevel 1 goto :failed
)
@echo off
cd ..
call scripts/run_gettext.bat
if errorlevel 1 goto :failed
cd %build_dir%
cmake --build . --target install --config %build_type%
if errorlevel 1 goto :failed

:done
@echo off
for /f "tokens=1-3 delims=:.," %%a in ("%_START_TIME: =0%") do set /a "_start_s=%%a*3600+%%b*60+%%c"
for /f "tokens=1-3 delims=:.," %%a in ("%TIME: =0%") do set /a "_end_s=%%a*3600+%%b*60+%%c"
set /a "_elapsed=_end_s - _start_s"
if %_elapsed% lss 0 set /a "_elapsed+=86400"
set /a "_hours=_elapsed / 3600"
set /a "_remainder=_elapsed - _hours * 3600"
set /a "_mins=_remainder / 60"
set /a "_secs=_remainder - _mins * 60"
echo.
echo Build completed in %_hours%h %_mins%m %_secs%s
exit /b 0

@REM A build step failed. Exit with its code so callers and CI see the
@REM failure; ERRORLEVEL must be captured before echo resets it.
:failed
set "_rc=%ERRORLEVEL%"
if "%_rc%"=="0" set "_rc=1"
echo.
echo Build FAILED with exit code %_rc%
exit /b %_rc%

set /a "_secs=_remainder - _mins * 60"
echo.
echo Build completed in %_hours%h %_mins%m %_secs%s

=== vs2022 ===
@REM OrcaSlicer build script for Windows
@echo off
set WP=%CD%

@REM Pack deps
if "%1"=="pack" (
    setlocal ENABLEDELAYEDEXPANSION 
    cd %WP%/deps/build
    for /f "tokens=2-4 delims=/ " %%a in ('date /t') do set build_date=%%c%%b%%a
    echo packing deps: OrcaSlicer_dep_win64_!build_date!_vs2022.zip

    %WP%/tools/7z.exe a OrcaSlicer_dep_win64_!build_date!_vs2022.zip OrcaSlicer_dep
    exit /b 0
)

set debug=OFF
set debuginfo=OFF
@REM Default target architecture to the host CPU arch; override with x64/arm64 arg.
set arch=x64
if /I "%PROCESSOR_ARCHITECTURE%"=="ARM64" set arch=ARM64
if /I "%PROCESSOR_ARCHITEW6432%"=="ARM64" set arch=ARM64
if "%1"=="debug" set debug=ON
if "%2"=="debug" set debug=ON
if "%1"=="debuginfo" set debuginfo=ON
if "%2"=="debuginfo" set debuginfo=ON
if /I "%1"=="arm64" set arch=ARM64
if /I "%2"=="arm64" set arch=ARM64
if /I "%1"=="x64" set arch=x64
if /I "%2"=="x64" set arch=x64
if "%debug%"=="ON" (
    set build_type=Debug
    set build_dir=build-dbg
) else (
    if "%debuginfo%"=="ON" (
        set build_type=RelWithDebInfo
        set build_dir=build-dbginfo
    ) else (
        set build_type=Release
        set build_dir=build
    )
)
if "%arch%"=="ARM64" set build_dir=%build_dir%-arm64
echo build type set to %build_type%, arch=%arch%

setlocal DISABLEDELAYEDEXPANSION 
cd deps
mkdir %build_dir%
cd %build_dir%
set "SIG_FLAG="
if defined ORCA_UPDATER_SIG_KEY set "SIG_FLAG=-DORCA_UPDATER_SIG_KEY=%ORCA_UPDATER_SIG_KEY%"

if "%1"=="slicer" (
    GOTO :slicer
)
echo "building deps.."

echo on
REM Set minimum CMake policy to avoid <3.5 errors
set CMAKE_POLICY_VERSION_MINIMUM=3.5
cmake ../ -G "Visual Studio 17 2022" -A %arch% -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=%build_type%
cmake --build . --config %build_type% --target deps -- -m
@echo off

if "%1"=="deps" exit /b 0

:slicer
echo "building Orca Slicer..."
cd %WP%
mkdir %build_dir%
cd %build_dir%

echo on
set CMAKE_POLICY_VERSION_MINIMUM=3.5
cmake .. -G "Visual Studio 17 2022" -A %arch% -DORCA_TOOLS=ON %SIG_FLAG% -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=%build_type%
cmake --build . --config %build_type% --target ALL_BUILD -- -m
@echo off
cd ..
call scripts/run_gettext.bat
cd %build_dir%
cmake --build . --target install --config %build_type%

Yes — three upstream batch files at the repo root, all inherited from OrcaSlicer:

| Script | What it does |
|---|---|
| [build_release_vs.bat](build_release_vs.bat) | The current one. Auto-detects VS version via `msbuild -version`, auto-detects x64/ARM64, optional `-x` for Ninja Multi-Config. This is what CI uses ([build_orca.yml:340](.github/workflows/build_orca.yml:340), [build_deps.yml:139](.github/workflows/build_deps.yml:139)). Your fork already touched it (`56eb9a1a Fail the Windows build script when a step fails`). |
| [build_release_vs2022.bat](build_release_vs2022.bat) | Older variant, hardcodes `Visual Studio 17 2022`. No msbuild detection, no fail-fast. |
| [build_release.bat](build_release.bat) | Oldest, hardcodes `Visual Studio 16 2019`. Effectively dead. |

All three take the same args: `deps` (deps only), `slicer` (skip deps), `debug` / `debuginfo`, `pack`. No arg = deps + slicer + gettext + install, Release, into `build\`.

**This machine is already provisioned and already has a full build.** VS 2022 Build Tools 17.14, CMake 4.3.5, Ninja, Strawberry Perl are installed; `deps\build\OrcaSlicer_dep` is populated and `build\OrcaSlicer\orca-slicer.exe` was built Sep 7 with the "Visual Studio 17 2022" / x64 / Release generator — i.e. someone already ran the vs2022 path here.

One gotcha: `msbuild` is **not** on PATH in this shell, so `build_release_vs.bat` will exit 1 at its version-detection step unless you launch from a VS Developer Command Prompt (or run `vcvars64.bat` first). Since deps are already built, the fastest incremental rebuild avoids the wrapper entirely:

```bash
cmake --build C:/src/JusPrin/build --config Release --target ALL_BUILD -- -m
```

If you want the wrapper's full flow (gettext + install into `build\OrcaSlicer\`), use the 2022 script, which doesn't need `msbuild` on PATH:

```bash
cd C:/src/JusPrin && ./build_release_vs2022.bat slicer
```

Found the real blocker — and it isn't the code.

`C:\src\JusPrin` and the entire `build\` tree are owned by `BUILTIN\Administrators`; `guitest` only has `ReadAndExecute` + `CreateFiles`. So new files can be created, but **existing** files can't be overwritten. The Sep 7 build was made by an elevated process, so CMake's regenerate step can't rewrite `cmake.check_cache`, `version.inc`, the `.rsp` files, or re-copy the deps DLLs. This session's token has Administrators marked *"deny only"* (UAC-filtered), and I can't elevate — that needs an interactive consent prompt.

Nothing compiled, so the branch is still unverified on Windows.

content.text:
Good choice — that makes this machine usable for agent-driven builds going forward.

Please run this in an **elevated** terminal (Win+X → *Terminal (Admin)*, or right-click PowerShell → *Run as administrator*):

```bash
icacls C:\src\JusPrin /grant "guitest:(OI)(CI)(M)" /T /C
```

What it does:
- `guitest:...(M)` — grants your account Modify (read/write/delete), not Full Control, so ownership and the existing SYSTEM/Administrators ACEs stay intact.
- `(OI)(CI)` — object- and container-inherit, so files and directories created later are writable too.
- `/T` — walks the existing tree, fixing the ~14GB of Administrator-owned build artifacts already there.
- `/C` — keeps going if a stray locked file errors out.

It'll print a lot of "processed file:" lines and take a minute or two on a tree this size; a few `Successfully processed N files; Failed processing 0 files` at the end is what you want.

Tell me when it's done and I'll rerun the incremental build against the existing `build\` tree and report whether the branch compiles.

Author: Kenneth Jiang <kenneth.jiang@gmail.com>
Date: Tue Sep 8 11:22:55 2026 -0700

# Count the changes you made by hand apart from the agent's

The setup card's "N changes from preset" said how far the project had
drifted but not who moved it, so a preset you had tuned yourself read as
the agent's work. Section 2e of the design answers that with "+ 2 yours"
in the eyebrow, beside an unchanged total.

AgentHost records the process settings the agent applies and the values
it applied them to. A change is the agent's only while that value is
still in force: edit the setting by hand and it becomes yours again,
because the card describes the project rather than the agent's turns.
Anything unprovable counts as yours -- crediting the agent for your edit
would make the card its opinion instead of the truth.

Three lifetimes fall out of that. Switching the process preset clears the
record, since the baseline every change is measured against has moved.
Reopening a project rebuilds it by replaying the persisted tool history,
without which a restart would relabel the agent's work as yours -- a loud
wrong claim rather than a quiet missing one. And the context is now
pushed once after both this write and the intent write, where before the
intent pushed and this did not, leaving the page showing new changes
under stale attribution.

The count is suppressed when every change is yours: "+ 7 yours" over
"7 changes from preset" is one fact twice, and the "+" claims an agent
contribution that is not there. While the agent is working it yields the
eyebrow, which the design reserves for one word at a time.

The eyebrow also stops wrapping. Measured in a browser at the dock's real
width -- around 310px in the running app, not the 429px design frame --
a three-digit count pushed "CURRENT SETUP" onto a second line and the
card silently grew a row. The heading gives up a few pixels to an
ellipsis instead.

Verified in the running application: a settings patch applied through the
tool bridge shows as the agent's, with no marker on the card and none on

entries.name: PushNotification
entries.description:
This tool sends a desktop notification in the user's terminal. If Remote Control is connected, it also pushes to their phone. Either way, it pulls their attention from whatever they're doing — a meeting, another task, dinner — to this session. That's the cost. The benefit is they learn something now that they'd want to know now: a long task finished while they were away, a build is ready, you've hit something that needs their decision before you can continue.

Because a notification they didn't need is annoying in a way that accumulates, err toward not sending one. Don't notify for routine progress, or to announce you've answered something they asked seconds ago and are clearly still watching, or when a quick task completes. Notify when there's a real chance they've walked away and there's something worth coming back for — or when they've explicitly asked you to notify them.

Keep the message under 200 characters, one line, no markdown. Lead with what they'd act on — "build failed: 2 auth tests" tells them more than "task done" and more than a status dump.

When the user is actively at the terminal, your output already reaches them — a notification on top of it would be a duplicate, so the tool skips it and says so. A "not sent" result is expected and only ever about this one notification: it was redundant, turned off, or had nowhere to go.

content.text:
Tests are running. Here's the finding while they go:

## The commit you pulled doesn't compile on Windows

[tests/agent/test_agent_bridge.cpp:1893](tests/agent/test_agent_bridge.cpp:1893) and [:1907](tests/agent/test_agent_bridge.cpp:1907) call `setenv`, which is POSIX — MSVC has no such function (`error C3861`). It builds on your Mac and dies here.

`setenv` is only the compile error. That one test case — *"mcp_connect runs an injected CLI runner"* — has three more POSIX assumptions that would still fail at **runtime** on Windows once it compiles:

| Line | Assumes | Windows needs |
|---|---|---|
| 1893 | `setenv(...)` | `_putenv_s` |
| 1892 | `":"` PATH separator | `';'` |
| 1888 | fixture named `claude` | `claude.exe` |

That list isn't guesswork — it's exactly what your own production code already does. [McpCatalog.cpp:52](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Mcp/McpCatalog.cpp:52) `command_on_path` branches on `_WIN32` to search for `command + ".exe"` split on `';'`. **The shipping code is portable; only the test is not.** So the test can't presently prove `command_on_path` works on the platform where its Windows branch actually runs.

There are no `#ifdef` guards anywhere in that file, so this is the sole compile blocker — every other suite built.

Two ways to go:

1. **Make the test portable** — a `_WIN32` branch mirroring `command_on_path`: `_putenv_s`, `';'`, and a `claude.exe` fixture. Small, and it makes the suite actually exercise the Windows path.
2. **Guard the test out on Windows** — smaller diff, but leaves `command_on_path`'s `_WIN32` branch untested on Windows, which is the branch most likely to break.

I'd go with (1); it's a few lines and buys real coverage. Want me to write it? I'll hold off touching your commit until you say.

Build and run the MCP CLI-runner test on Windows

The test reached for setenv, which is POSIX; MSVC has no such function, so
agent_bridge_tests failed to compile and CMake registered the suite as
NOT_BUILT. All 166 of its cases were silently absent from every Windows
run, not merely the one that used setenv.

Compiling was necessary but not sufficient. The fixture is discovered by
McpCatalog::command_on_path, which dresses the command per platform:
"claude.exe" found along a ';'-split PATH under Windows, bare "claude"
along a ':'-split one elsewhere. A test that writes "claude" and joins
with ':' builds cleanly and then fails, because the search looks for a
name it never created. The three assumptions travel together, so the
platform split names all three beside each other and points at the
production function that dictates them.

Guarding the case out of Windows was the smaller change and the wrong
one: command_on_path's Windows branch is the half no one exercises, and
skipping the test there would leave it that way.

Verified on Windows: agent_bridge_tests compiles, and the case passes
with 5 assertions, resolving claude.exe through a ';'-split PATH. The
suite total goes from 246 to 412 tests once it is built.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF

Committed as `9e0247cc`, working tree clean. Not pushed — say the word if you want that.

## Final state

| | Result |
|---|---|
| C++ app build | Pass — exit 0 |
| TypeScript (vitest) | 113/113 |

Fixing the compile break took the suite from 246 to 412 tests — **166 agent tests had never run on Windows at all**, silently registered as `NOT_BUILT` rather than reported as missing.

## Two failures remain, neither from my change

**1. PlaceholderParser segfault** — the pre-existing one you told me to skip. Untouched.

**2. `MCP discovery publication is atomic and private`** — newly revealed by getting the suite to build. This one is worth your attention, and it is **not** a test bug:

[test_mcp_discovery.cpp:36](tests/agent/test_mcp_discovery.cpp:36) spins a reader thread calling `Mcp::read_discovery` while the main thread does 50 `write_discovery` calls, then asserts the reader never saw a missing file. On Windows it dies with `0xc0000409` — a fail-fast, consistent with an exception escaping the reader thread rather than a failed assertion.

The test is already correctly Windows-aware (it `#ifndef _WIN32`s the POSIX permission check at line 49). So the finger points at the production code in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Mcp/` — the write-temp-then-rename publication that is atomic on POSIX likely isn't on Windows, where a rename over an existing file can fail outright and readers can hit a transiently unavailable file.

If that reading is right, it's a genuine Windows defect in shipping code, not test scaffolding — the discovery file could briefly vanish for a real client. I haven't confirmed it; that needs a look at `write_discovery`. Want me to dig in?

content.text:
Probe removed, tree clean, test binary rebuilding without it. Here's what I found.

## What's wrong

The MCP discovery file is a little file JusPrin writes so other programs can find it. The code updates it the careful way: write a new copy to a side file, then swap it into place in one move, so nobody ever sees a half-written file.

**On Windows that swap fails as soon as anything is reading the file.** Windows refuses with "Access is denied."

It's not a rare race. In my test it failed after a *single* read — basically the first instant a reader had the file open.

## How I know

The crash leaves a mess behind, and the mess tells the story: every crashed run left exactly one leftover side file, complete and correct at 251 bytes. So writing worked fine. Only the swap failed.

I then wrote a throwaway probe that caught the error instead of crashing, and it named it outright: `Publish MCP discovery: Access is denied.` I've since deleted the probe.

## Why it crashes so violently

When the swap fails, the code raises an error. The test that was running had a background thread going at the time, and that thread was never shut down before the error escaped. Windows responds by killing the whole process instantly — no message, no failure report, just a hard exit. That's why the test output was blank.

That part is the test's fault. The failed swap underneath it is not.

## What this means for the real app

The same function runs at JusPrin startup — it's called while constructing `McpRuntime`, in the member initializer list, which is the worst possible spot: if it throws there, the object never finishes building.

I want to be straight about the limits of what I've shown. I proved the swap fails **when another reader has the file open**. At startup, on a normal machine, usually nothing else is reading it yet, which is likely why this has never bitten you. The realistic triggers are a second JusPrin running, an editor or antivirus touching the file, or a client polling it. I have not tested those, so I can't tell you how often it happens in practice.

What I can say is that the design's central promise — that this update is safe while others are reading — does not hold on Windows.

## Worth knowing

The rest of that code is genuinely well built for Windows. Readers already open the file in the special mode that's *supposed* to permit exactly this kind of swap, and the swap uses the right Windows call. Somebody thought about this carefully. The chosen call just doesn't behave the way it looks like it should. Windows has a different function meant for replacing files that are currently open, which is likely the fix.

Two things I have **not** done: fixed this, or touched the separate PlaceholderParser crash you told me to skip. Say the word if you want the fix.

+// target that any process holds open fails with ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED, and
+// readers hold it open constantly by design. Sharing delete access does not

+// handles keep reading the file they already opened.
+// It needs NTFS and Windows 10 1607, so the caller falls back to the ordinary
+// replace rather than refusing to publish on a volume that cannot do this.
+bool rename_over_open_readers(const fs::path& temporary, const fs::path& path, DWORD& error)

cd C:/src/JusPrin; git commit -F - <<'EOF'
Publish MCP discovery without breaking on open readers

Replacing the discovery record used MoveFileExW, which fails with
ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED the moment any process holds the target open. Readers
hold it open constantly by design, so the publish did not merely race --
it failed almost immediately, after a single read in a loop of fifty
writes. Sharing delete access does not rescue the ordinary rename, and
the write_discovery contract of a reader never seeing a partial record
could not be honoured on Windows at all.

FileRenameInfoEx with POSIX semantics is the rename that behaves like
rename(2): the name is rebound at once while existing handles keep
reading the file they already opened. It needs NTFS and Windows 10 1607,
so a volume that cannot do it falls back to the previous replace rather
than refusing to publish, leaving those cases no worse than before.

The failure was invisible until now because agent_bridge_tests did not
compile on Windows. Once it did, the atomicity test took the process
down with it: write_discovery threw, the throw escaped a scope holding a
joinable reader thread, and the std::thread destructor called
std::terminate. Windows reports that as a bare 0xC0000409 fast-fail with
no Catch2 output, which is why a real defect looked like a crashing test.
That fragility is left alone here; it stops mattering once the publish
succeeds.

Verified on Windows: the atomicity test passed fifteen consecutive runs
having previously failed every one, and ctest reports one failure out of
414, the pre-existing PlaceholderParser segfault this does not touch.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
git log --oneline -2

Committed as `ad7376f7`, one file only.

## Done

| | Result |
|---|---|
| Full build | Clean — exit 0, zero errors |
| ctest | **413/414** |
| Commits | `9e0247cc` (setenv fix), `ad7376f7` (discovery fix) — neither pushed |

The only failing test is the PlaceholderParser segfault you told me to leave.

**The fix:** `write_discovery` now uses `FileRenameInfoEx` with POSIX semantics, which rebinds the filename while existing readers keep reading — the Windows equivalent of `rename(2)`. It falls back to the old `MoveFileExW` where that isn't available (non-NTFS, pre-Win10-1607), so those cases are no worse than before. That test went from failing every run to 15/15 clean.

## Someone else is actively working in this repo

This needs your attention. Since I last checked, the foreign changes have grown well beyond the one file:

```

 M tests/shell/CMakeLists.txt

?? resources/jusprin/agent/.gitattributes
?? src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/.gitattributes

```

I retracted the "concurrent activity" theory earlier when the process evidence turned out to be my own build. That retraction was wrong — there was no competing *build*, but there is clearly another session *editing*. I should have separated those two claims instead of dropping both.

This matters for my numbers: the suite grew 412 → 414 because their new `test_host_locale.cpp` added tests. My final run therefore validated a tree containing their in-progress work. My own fix's verification stands on its own — the discovery and agent tests don't touch their files — but the 413/414 figure describes a mixed tree, not your committed state.

All of it is left uncommitted, per your call. Worth checking whether that other session is one you meant to have running.
